paragraphs.text: monitoring temperature, frequence, memory usage of both cpu and gpu for local IA usage
# DSH Local Monitor

A floating, draggable sensor dashboard for the **DeepSeek Harness** Web UI:
GPU readings from **GPU-
Z** on the left, CPU and system memory on the right.
Six live cards in one compact window:
| Left column — GPU | Right column — CPU |

| GPU temperature | CPU temperature |
| GPU clock | CPU clock |
| Dedicated VRAM in use (with a /16
GB bar) | System memory in use (with a /32 GB bar) |

The window can be dragged anywhere by its title bar, remembers its position
across reloads, collapse

s to a single header row, and follows the app theme
(light and dark). Labels are bilingual: French w

hen the app locale or the
browser is French, English otherwise.
## Features

- **Live by default** — the Host samples every second, the window refreshes
every 1.5 s; a status do

t shows *live* vs *offline*.
- **Real GPU-Z data** — reads the `GPUZShMem` shared-memory block GPU-Z

publishes while it runs (the exact numbers of its *Sensors* tab), no OCR and
no screen scraping.
-

**Floating and draggable** — rendered into the frame-wide `shell.overlay`
slot, so it sits above eve

ry column without stealing clicks elsewhere.
- **Theme-aware** — every colour is a Harness theme tok

en, so it reads correctly
in light and dark themes.
- **No dependencies** — plain React from the bro

wser module table, and a single
long-lived PowerShell child on the Host side.
## Data sources
| Value | Source |
| GPU temperature, GPU clock, dedicated VRAM used / total, card name | GPU-Z shared memory (`GPUZShm

em`) |
| CPU temperature | GPU-Z's `CPU Temperature` sensor when it publishes one; otherwise the ACP

I thermal zone (labelled "motherboard zone") |
| CPU clock and load | Windows performance data (`Win

32_PerfFormattedData_Counters_ProcessorInformation`) |
| System memory in use | `GlobalMemoryStatusE

erfFormattedData_Counters_ProcessorInformation`) |
| System memory in use | `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` |
## Requirements

- **Windows 10/11** — the collector uses the Windows sensor APIs.
- **GPU-Z running** — download it

from TechPowerUp.
If GPU-Z is not running, the GPU column shows *"GPU-Z not found"* and the rest
kee

ps working.
- **DeepSeek Harness** with a web profile.

## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- `index.js` (Host) spawns `helper.ps1`, parses its JSON lines, keeps the latest
sample in memory an

d exposes it as read-only JSON on
`/dsh-local-monitor/sensors.json`. The route accepts loopback, sam

e-origin
requests only. The child is restarted automatically if it exits.
- `helper.ps1` runs one sa

mpling loop: GPU-Z shared memory, CPU temperature and
clock, physical memory. One JSON object per li

ne on stdout.
- `client.js` (browser) registers a `shell.overlay` entry (`id:
dsh-local-monitor`) an

lient.js` (browser) registers a `shell.overlay` entry (`id:
dsh-local-monitor`) and polls the route.
## Tuning
Two constants at the top of `client.js`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`VSCALE` compresses paddings, gaps, card heights and line heights only — glyph
sizes and the width s

esses paddings, gaps, card heights and line heights only — glyph
sizes and the width stay untouched.

The sampling interval lives in `helper.ps1` (`$intervalMs = 1000`) and the poll
interval in `client.
js` (`POLL_MS = 1500`).
## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Fix |
| Window does not appear | Reload with `Ctrl+Shift+R`; check the plugin is enabled in Settings → Plu

gins. |
| GPU column shows "GPU-Z not found" | Start GPU-Z (it may stay minimized in the tray). |
|
CPU temperature says "motherboard zone" | GPU-Z is not publishing its CPU sensor on this machine; th

e value then comes from the ACPI zone and is approximate. |
| Numbers frozen on screen | The status
dot shows *offline* when the Host has no fresh sample: check that `powershell.exe` can start and tha

t GPU-Z is alive. |
| Nothing at all / route 404 | The Host half failed to load — check the Host log
for `dsh-local-monitor`. |
